title_en: Hu Tianyun v. Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng — dispute over ownership confirmation
ruling_gist_en: The housing demolition resettlement rights are comprehensive powers of house ownership, generally including compensation for the demolished house, relocation expenses, subsidies for new house construction, land use rights for new house construction, etc. The attribution of demolition resettlement rights shall be determined by the ownership of the demolished house. Co-owners have the right to divide such rights through an agreement.

full_text_en:
Hu Tianyun v. Tang Jinqin, Wang Jianfeng — Dispute over Ownership Confirmation

Ruling Summary

The housing demolition and resettlement rights are comprehensive rights appertaining to the ownership of the house, generally including compensation for the demolished house, relocation expenses, subsidies for the new house, and the right to use the land for the new house. The attribution of the resettlement rights following demolition shall be determined by the ownership of the demolished house, and co-owners may, by agreement, divide such rights.

Where a house is constructed on land over which another person has the right of use, thereby forming an attachment, the ownership of the house generally belongs to the holder of the land use right. The compensation to be made to the person who actually constructed the house and who is not the holder of the land use right includes not only monetary payment but also, in the context of a specific personal relationship, the right to reside in and use the house.

Plaintiff: Hu Tianyun, female, 39 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Fuxing Village, Lianhua District, Yunjian Street, Lanxi City.

Defendants: Tang Jinqin, male, 44 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Fuxing Village, Lianhua District, Yunjian Street, Lanxi City.

Defendant: Wang Jianfeng, female, 40 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Houfan Village, Lianhua District, Yunjian Street, Lanxi City.

The plaintiff, Hu Tianyun, filed a lawsuit with the Lanxi People's Court of Zhejiang Province against the defendants, Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng, over a dispute concerning the confirmation of ownership.

Plaintiff's Allegations:

The defendant Wang Jianfeng is the former wife of the defendant Tang Jinqin. They divorced in January 2000, and made the following agreements regarding the house located at No. 13 Caojia Road, Huanglongdong, Lanxi City, and the custody of their child: the house consisted of two units and three floors; the first and third floors belonged to Tang Jinqin, and the second floor belonged to Wang Jianfeng. Their biological son, Tang Hongbo, was to be raised by Tang Jinqin. In the event of demolition compensation, Wang Jianfeng was to receive one-third. The plaintiff, after her own divorce, married Tang Jinqin on March 26, 2004. In July 2006, the house at No. 13 Caojia Road was demolished due to road widening and renovation, yielding a total of over 270,000 yuan in various compensations. Pursuant to the divorce agreement, Wang Jianfeng received 90,000 yuan in demolition compensation from the Lanxi Demolition Office, and the remainder was collected by Tang Jinqin. Subsequently, the plaintiff and Tang Jinqin jointly funded the construction of a house located at No. 1, Building 27, Fuxing Village, Lianhua District, Yunjian Street, Lanxi City, and lived there together with Tang Jinqin, Tang Hongbo, and the plaintiff's son. Around October 2009, Wang Jianfeng, claiming that the house built by the plaintiff belonged jointly to Tang Hongbo and Tang Jinqin, requested the village committee to mediate and divide the real property belonging to Tang Hongbo individually. It was at this point that the plaintiff learned that Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng had already reached an agreement on the division of the newly built property. Because the plaintiff believed that the agreement infringed upon her rights, the mediation failed. In June 2010, Tang Hongbo, Tang Jinqin's son, filed a lawsuit requesting the court to confirm that the third and fourth floors of the house at No. 1, Building 27, Fuxing Village, Lianhua District, Yunjian Street, Lanxi City belonged to him. The plaintiff argued that the property rights of Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng had already been demolished by the government, and that Wang Jianfeng had already collected her compensation, thus she had no right to dispose of the house at No. 1, Building 27, Fuxing Village, Lianhua District, Yunjian Street, Lanxi City, which belonged jointly to the plaintiff and Tang Jinqin. The plaintiff requested that the court declare invalid Clause 3 of the agreement concerning the division of demolition compensation and property rights entered into by Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng on July 8, 2006.

The plaintiff, Hu Tianyun, submitted the following evidence:

1. Plaintiff Hu Tianyun's identity card, proving her identity.
2. Marriage certificate, proving that plaintiff Hu Tianyun and defendant Tang Jinqin registered their marriage in 2004.
3. Divorce certificate and divorce agreement, proving the divorce of defendant Wang Jianfeng and defendant Tang Jinqin in 2000, and their agreements on property division and child custody at the time of divorce.
4. Agreement on compensation and resettlement for demolition of a house on collective land, proving that the house at No. 13 Caojia Road, Lanxi City, was demolished and that the total compensation received was 280,498 yuan.
5. An agreement, proving the agreement between defendant Wang Jianfeng and defendant Tang Jinqin regarding the division of the newly built house.

Defendant Tang Jinqin's Defense:

Tang Jinqin and defendant Wang Jianfeng divorced in 2000, and at that time agreed that the second floor of the two-unit, three-story house belonged to Wang Jianfeng. Tang Jinqin married plaintiff Hu Tianyun in 2004. Before the house was demolished, Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng signed an agreement in the village, stipulating that the first and second floors of the newly built house would belong to Tang Jinqin, and the third floor and above would belong to their son Tang Hongbo. Out of fear of being blamed, Tang Jinqin did not inform Hu Tianyun of the terms of this agreement. The compensation Tang Jinqin received amounted to 180,000 yuan, of which over 20,000 yuan was used to repay debts remaining from the old house, and the remainder was used for building the new house, which cost approximately 300,000 yuan.

Defendant Wang Jianfeng's Defense:

Pursuant to the divorce agreement, plaintiff Hu Tianyun had no ownership interest in the demolished house. Pursuant to the oral agreement between Wang Jianfeng and defendant Tang Jinqin at the time of divorce, because their son Tang Hongbo was to be raised by Tang Jinqin, the first and third floors of the demolished house belonged to Tang Jinqin, with one floor belonging to their son. The second floor belonged to Wang Jianfeng. The demolition compensation for the house also included a share for their son. The old two-unit, three-story house was built together with others, and indeed a sum of money was borrowed. In 2006, after the house was scheduled for demolition, Wang Jianfeng requested that the son's share be separately listed, otherwise she would build her own house. Tang Jinqin disagreed. Subsequently, with the village committee's seal affixed as a witness, the two parties signed an agreement on the distribution of demolition and resettlement rights.

Facts Found by the Lanxi People's Court at First Instance:

Defendants Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng were originally husband and wife. The house originally located at No. 13 Caojia Road, Lanxi City, consisting of two units and three floors, was their joint property. They agreed to divorce in January 2000. The divorce agreement stipulated: the son Tang Hongbo would be raised by Tang Jinqin. Regarding the jointly owned property of two units of the house, the second floor would belong to Wang Jianfeng, and the first and third floors would belong to Tang Jinqin. The stairwell would be used by both parties. If the house were demolished, one-third of the economic compensation would be given to Wang Jianfeng. In March 2004, Tang Jinqin registered his marriage with plaintiff Hu Tianyun. In July 2006, the house at No. 13 Caojia Road, consisting of two units and three floors, was required to be demolished due to the widening of Caojia Road. The local village committee arranged a foundation for building a new house. Wang Jianfeng requested to participate in building the house, but Tang Jinqin disagreed with jointly constructing it. After negotiations, on July 8, 2006, the two parties signed an agreement with the local village committee as witness. Clause 3 concerning the division of housing stipulated: If a foundation is arranged for building a new house, it shall be built by Tang Jinqin (the house cannot be lower than three floors). After completion, the house shall not be sold, mortgaged, or transferred. The first and second floors shall belong to Tang Jinqin, and the floors above the second floor shall belong to Tang Hongbo. The stairwell shall be used jointly by both parties. After Tang Jinqin's death, the first and second floors belonging to him shall pass to the lawful heir, Tang Hongbo. On July 21, 2006, Lanxi Jianye House Demolition Co., Ltd. signed an agreement on compensation and resettlement for demolition of a house on collective land with Tang Jinqin. Pursuant to their agreement, Wang Jianfeng received 90,000 yuan in house demolition compensation. Tang Jinqin built a house on the land arranged by the village, currently located at No. 1, Building 27, Fuxing Village, Lianhua New District, Lanxi City. In June 2010, Tang Hongbo, Tang Jinqin's son, filed a lawsuit with the court requesting confirmation that the third and fourth floors of the house at No. 1, Building 27, Fuxing Village, Lianhua District, Yunjian Street, Lanxi City, belonged to him.

Opinion of the Lanxi People's Court at First Instance:

The house originally located at No. 13 Caojia Road, Lanxi City, consisting of two units and three floors, was the joint property of defendants Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng. The compensation received after the demolition of the house and the new house built on the land arranged by the village represent a transformation of the form of the property. Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng had the right to dispose of their own property. The agreement they signed was a true expression of the intentions of Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng. Although the disputed house was built after the marriage of plaintiff Hu Tianyun and Tang Jinqin, Hu Tianyun failed to provide evidence of her contribution to the construction costs. Her claim that the agreement between Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng infringed upon her lawful rights and interests lacked sufficient evidence.

Accordingly, the Lanxi People's Court of Zhejiang Province, pursuant to Article 1 and Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, and Article 58 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on October 27, 2010:

The claims of the plaintiff, Hu Tianyun, are dismissed.

Hu Tianyun appealed against the first-instance judgment to the Jinhua Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province. Her main grounds of appeal were:

1. Of the demolished two-unit, three-story house at No. 13 Caojia Road, only the two rooms on the second floor and one room on the third floor were the jointly owned property of the respondents Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng; the remainder was Tang Jinqin's pre-marital property. The division of these properties at the time of their divorce already favored Wang Jianfeng.
2. Wang Jianfeng had already received her full share of the demolition compensation and foundation reconstruction fee totaling 90,000 yuan, and therefore had no right to make any claim regarding the new house co-built by the appellant and Tang Jinqin.
3. The demolition and resettlement agreement reached between Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng was unilaterally drafted by Wang Jianfeng. She used village cadres to force Tang Jinqin to sign it, thereby completely depriving the appellant of her lawful property rights. The agreement was illegal and void.
4. The original house and the newly built house after demolition are two distinctly different property ownerships. The original house, under the divorce agreement, belonged jointly to Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng, but the new house built after its demolition belongs to the appellant and Tang Jinqin as marital property.
5. In the second instance, the appellant will provide evidence of the funds contributed to building the new house, totaling 322,351 yuan.

In light of the above, the appellant requested that the original judgment be overturned and a new judgment be entered in her favor.

The appellant, Hu Tianyun, submitted the following evidence in the second instance:

1. A written statement from He Linshu, proving that three rooms in the pre-demolition house were sold by He Linshu in March 1996 for 38,000 yuan to the respondents Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng.
2. A total of 14 documents, including loan certificates, IOUs, and payment receipts, collectively proving that the appellant Hu Tianyun and the respondent Tang Jinqin invested 322,351 yuan in the construction of the new house, of which the appellant contributed 104,797 yuan.
3. A house number plate certificate, proving the location of the new house co-built by the appellant Hu Tianyun and the respondent Tang Jinqin.

In his response, the respondent Tang Jinqin argued that of the demolished two-unit, three-story house at No. 13 Caojia Road, only the two rooms on the second floor and one room on the third floor were the jointly owned property of Tang Jinqin and the respondent Wang Jianfeng; the two rooms on the first floor and one room on the third floor were built jointly with his mother, and his mother's consent was not obtained when the property was divided at the time of his divorce from Wang Jianfeng.

In her response, the respondent Wang Jianfeng argued that because she had a one-third share in the old house, under the demolition policy she was entitled to re-obtain a foundation for building a house. Pursuant to the agreement on demolition and resettlement with the respondent Tang Jinqin, she did not participate in building the house; however, the construction activities of Tang Jinqin and the appellant Hu Tianyun involved her land use rights. Wang Jianfeng signed the demolition and resettlement agreement with Tang Jinqin solely to protect the interests of their mutual biological son.

In the second instance, the respondent Wang Jianfeng submitted a written statement from Tang Jianhua, the brother of the respondent Tang Jinqin, proving that the demolished house belonged to Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng and was unrelated to their mother, Tong Xiulian.

The Jinhua Intermediate People's Court, after the second instance, confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

Issues in Dispute in the Second Instance:

1. The ownership of the two-unit, three-story house at No. 13 Caojia Road, Huanglongdong Village, Lanxi City.
2. The attribution and division of the demolition and resettlement rights.
3. Whether the appellant, Hu Tianyun, could claim ownership of the house based on her involvement in its construction.

Opinion of the Jinhua Intermediate People's Court at Second Instance:

1. Concerning the first issue in dispute.

The evidence submitted by the appellant Hu Tianyun (Exhibit 1) and the evidence submitted by the respondent Wang Jianfeng both concern the ownership of the demolished house. The unrelated interested party involved is Tong Xiulian, the mother of the respondent Tang Jinqin, which is irrelevant to the appellant Hu Tianyun. Furthermore, Tong Xiulian has not raised any objection to the division of ownership of the demolished house as stipulated in the divorce agreement between Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng reached in 1999. The compensation and resettlement agreement for the house demolition was also signed and performed by Tang Jinqin. Therefore, in this case, the divorce agreement shall serve as the basis for determining the ownership of the demolished house, and it can be confirmed that the two-unit, three-story house located at No. 13 Caojia Road, Huanglongdong Village, Lanxi City, was jointly owned by Wang Jianfeng and Tang Jinqin.

2. Concerning the second issue in dispute.

In accordance with the inherent legal attributes of real property ownership and the generally applicable policy provisions in the process of housing demolition and resettlement, resettlement rights are comprehensive rights appertaining to the ownership of the house, generally including compensation for the demolished house, relocation expenses, subsidies for the new house, and the right to use the land for the new house. Because the divorce agreement between the respondent Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng concluded in 1999 stipulated that the two-unit, three-story house located at No. 13 Caojia Road, Huanglongdong Village, Lanxi City, was jointly owned by them, the demolition and resettlement rights derived from the ownership of that house belonged jointly to Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng. They were entitled to negotiate and determine the specific implementation and distribution of the resettlement rights. Examining the process of signing the agreement on the distribution of resettlement rights, although Wang Jianfeng initially claimed to independently enjoy the resettlement rights, particularly the right to use the land for the new house, after jointly deciding to dispose of the post-resettlement new house in a manner that protected the interests of their mutual biological son Tang Hongbo, she agreed that Tang Jinqin would solely enjoy the right to use the land for the new house. The other components of the resettlement rights were to be enjoyed by her based on the basic principle of one-third. Therefore, the overall interests in the agreement on the distribution of resettlement rights reached by Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng were balanced and did not constitute any obvious unfairness.

3. Concerning the third issue in dispute.

Because the respondent Tang Jinqin was to exclusively enjoy the right to use the land for the new house — meaning the respondent Wang Jianfeng withdrew from the construction of the new house — the appellant Hu Tianyun, as Tang Jinqin's current wife, was necessarily involved in the construction. However, given that Hu Tianyun and Tang Jinqin did not dispute the fact that over 160,000 yuan in various demolition and resettlement compensation was invested in the construction of the resettlement house, and considering the statements made by the Party secretary and the village director of Huanglongdong Village in the first-instance court investigation record regarding the construction cost per square meter of the resettlement house, the construction of the resettlement house did not require any significant additional investment. Moreover, the key factor determining the ownership of the resettlement house is the land use right, not the construction cost. Additionally, half of the additional investment was subject to Tang Jinqin's right of disposal. Therefore, although Hu Tianyun made a certain contribution to the house in dispute in this case, it was insufficient to establish her right to a share of the ownership of the house, and that contribution was essentially equivalent to the right to reside in and use the house that she enjoyed. Consequently, the agreement on the distribution of resettlement rights reached by Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng did not harm the lawful rights and interests of Hu Tianyun.

In conclusion, the appellant Hu Tianyun's grounds for claiming the invalidity of Clause 3 of the agreement on the distribution of demolition and resettlement rights entered into by the respondents Tang Jinqin and Wang Jianfeng on July 8, 2006, are all untenable. Accordingly, the Jinhua Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on January 13, 2011:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
